level.description: What if you didn't even have to rent the server? Welcome to the water faucet model of cloud computing.

quiz_data.question: What is the defining feature of Serverless Architecture?

lessons.title: The Water Faucet Metaphor
lessons.content_md:
# The Water Faucet Metaphor 🚰

When you use IaaS (like renting a Virtual Machine), you pay by the hour. If you rent a server for 24 hours, you pay for 24 hours of electricity and hardware, even if absolutely nobody visited your website while you were asleep.

This is like paying for water by renting an entire water tower for the month, even if you only drank one glass!

## The Serverless Revolution

**Serverless** computing changes everything. Instead of renting the server, you just write a small piece of code (a function) and give it to the Cloud provider.

You say: *"Hey Amazon, please run this code ONLY when someone clicks the 'Buy' button on my app."*

When a customer clicks the button, Amazon instantly turns the code on, runs it, and turns it off. 

**You only pay for the exact milliseconds your code was running.**

If no one clicks the button for a week, you pay **$0.00**. This is exactly like your kitchen sink: you only pay for water when the faucet is actively running!

<flipcard front="🚰 What is the main cost benefit of Serverless?" back="You only pay for the exact milliseconds your code is actively running. If there is no traffic, you pay absolutely nothing! (No idle server costs)."></flipcard>

lessons.title: Functions as a Service (FaaS)
lessons.content_md:
# Functions as a Service (FaaS) ⚡

Wait, why is it called "Serverless"? Are there no servers?

No, there are definitely still physical servers in a data center. It's called "Serverless" because **YOU** don't have to think about them, manage them, or pay for them when they are idle.

The technical term for this is **FaaS (Functions as a Service)**.

## How FaaS Works

1. A developer writes a tiny block of code (a Function). For example: a function that resizes an image.
2. They upload it to AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Functions, or Azure Functions.
3. They set a **Trigger**. (e.g., "Run this function every time a user uploads a photo").
4. If 10,000 users upload a photo at the exact same second, the Cloud provider instantly spins up 10,000 copies of the function, runs them all simultaneously, and then shuts them all down.

<flipcard front="⚡ What does FaaS stand for?" back="Functions as a Service! It allows developers to deploy small snippets of code that automatically scale infinitely without managing any servers."></flipcard>
